world.bio: I am a Frenchman running the wine list at a Bund restaurant for nine years. My kids' international school just raised fees by 20 percent and I am weighing whether to move them to a local bilingual school I know nothing about. I am learning Chinese characters but stuck around 600, my back hurts from carrying cases up cellar stairs, and I play five-a-side football on Thursdays.
skills_assets: Court of Master Sommeliers advanced certificate, nine years running a wine list of about 600 labels
Cellar management: inventory, rotation, temperature control, supplier negotiation
A network of importers and wine merchants in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Bordeaux
Fluent French and English, conversational Mandarin
Personal wine collection of about 200 bottles

projects.name: School decision
projects.text: The kids' international school announced fees up 20 percent next year. Two kids, 9 and 12, so the increase is close to 100,000 RMB per year. A local bilingual school in Pudong has been recommended by a colleague, but I have never been inside one and I do not know how to judge it. The deadline for the deposit is in November.

projects.name: Wine list autumn refresh
projects.text: Restaurant management wants a refreshed list for the Christmas season. I'm tasting with importers twice a week and trying to bring a few smaller producers from the Loire and Jura without raising the average bottle price.

notes.text: Back to the cellar. Carried six cases up the stairs and felt something pull in my lower back. Spent the rest of the shift standing very straight. The chef asked if I had been drinking. I said it was the opposite.
The school letter arrived in my daughter's bag. Fees up 20 percent. Anna read it over my shoulder and said, 'Papa, are we poor now?' I said no. Then I did the math at night and it was not nothing.

Tasted with an importer from Burgundy. He wanted to push a new Chablis at a price I could not justify. I told him, politely, that people in Shanghai want a story more than a label. He looked disappointed, which is fair.
Chinese lessons. My teacher gave me 'bei' and 'zhong' and 'shu'. I wrote each of them twenty times. At home my son watched me and said, 'Papa, your characters look like a drunk spider.' I laughed.
Football on Thursday. Scored one goal, missed an open net, got shouted at in three languages. My knee is complaining but I feel alive.

Colleague mentioned a local bilingual school in Pudong. Said it is rigorous, strong in math, much cheaper. I looked at the website, all in Chinese. I could read maybe forty percent of it. I need someone to tell me what it is really like.
Wife asked what we are doing about school. I said we will decide by November. She said, 'You always say that.' I said it is a big decision. She said, 'Yes, so decide.'
A guest at table seven asked for a 'natural wine from Jura' and I poured him a Savagnin. He closed his eyes and smiled. These moments are why I do this job.

Visited the bookshop in the French Concession and bought a children's book in Chinese, hoping to read it with my kids. We got through two pages before my son took the book and read it himself, fluently. Humbling.

messages.text:
Lily: Etienne, can you finalise the Christmas wine list by the end of October?
Me: I'm on it. I want to add two small Jura producers.
Lily: Fine, as long as margins hold.

Claire: School fees. Please tell me you've thought about it.
Me: I've thought about nothing else.
Claire: Then talk to the other parents.

Marc: Thursday, 8pm, pitch two.
Me: Count me in.
Marc: Bring your good knee.

Wei: The Pudong school I mentioned, they have an open day on the 17th.
Me: In English or Chinese?
Wei: Chinese, mostly. You might need someone to translate.

Importer: Etienne, the new vintage is ready. 30 cases.
Me: Let me taste first.
Importer: Of course.
